answer: Every agent must lock a bond before trading, and peers attest only to agents they have transacted with. A new persona starts in a cold tundra of zero reputation, so its first trades are costly to fake. A sybil farm cannot act like a lone falcon that strikes once and vanishes; it must keep thousands of puppets alive, paying stake and upkeep. Slashing a proven duplicate burns the whole bond, so the attacker loses real capital whenever a cluster is exposed. Attestation paths work like saffron dye, letting honest agents route payments along verified lineages and starving fake identities of income.
